# Contract: theme variables derived from the application's tokens

`crates/micold-core/src/tokens/css.rs` emits this sheet; `site/theme/css/site.css` consumes it and
contains no literal of its own. This file is the contract between the two (FR-030, SC-014).

## Shape of the emitted file

```css
/* GENERATED by micold-tokens-css from crates/micold-core/src/tokens/. Do not edit. */
:root { /* light scheme */
  --micold-primary: #6750a4;
  --micold-surface: #fef7ff;
  /* … */
}
:root[data-scheme="dark"] { /* dark scheme — same names, dark values */
  --micold-primary: #d0bcff;
  /* … */
}
```

One name per token, defined in both blocks. A name defined in one block and not the other is a bug
in the emitter, not a design choice.

## Naming

`--micold-<group>-<token>`, kebab-cased from the token's own identifier. The identifier is the
contract: renaming a token in `micold-core` renames the variable, `site.css` fails to find it, and
the site build fails — which is the intended coupling. A variable that quietly falls back to an
initial value would be the derivation failing silently.

| Group | Prefix | Source | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colour roles | `--micold-` | `tokens::Roles` | `--micold-primary`, `--micold-on-surface`, `--micold-surface-container-high`, `--micold-outline-variant` |
| Type scale | `--micold-type-` | `tokens/typography.rs` | `--micold-type-body-medium-size`, `--micold-type-title-large-weight`, `--micold-type-label-small-line-height` |
| Shape | `--micold-shape-` | `tokens/shape.rs` | `--micold-shape-corner-small`, `--micold-shape-corner-extra-large` |
| Elevation | `--micold-elevation-` | `tokens/elevation.rs` | `--micold-elevation-1` (a complete `box-shadow` value), `--micold-elevation-1-surface` (the tint that accompanies it) |
| Spacing | `--micold-spacing-` | `tokens/mod.rs` (`mod spacing`) | `--micold-spacing-xs` … `--micold-spacing-xl` |
| Motion | `--micold-motion-` | `tokens/motion.rs` | `--micold-motion-duration-short`, `--micold-motion-easing-emphasized` |
| State | `--micold-state-` | `tokens/state.rs` | `--micold-state-hover-opacity`, `--micold-state-pressed-opacity` |

The scrim is a pair — `--micold-scrim` and `--micold-scrim-opacity` — because a scrim is a colour
used at an opacity, and a site that hard-coded the opacity would drift from the application's the
first time it changed.

Units are emitted, not left to the consumer: colours as `#rrggbb`, sizes in `px`, durations in `ms`,
easings as complete `cubic-bezier(...)`, elevations as complete `box-shadow` values.

## What the site is allowed to do with them

**Permitted** — the two treatments FR-029a names, plus ordinary documentation furniture:

- the header is the application's top app bar: its surface role, its elevation, its title type;
- panels (the table of contents, code blocks, callouts, figures) are separated by surface shade and
  elevation, never by an outline;
- outlines appear in exactly the three places the application uses them: a divider, the border of an
  outlined control, and the focus indicator;
- transitions use `--micold-motion-*`, and are removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
  (FR-030b).

**Forbidden**:

- any literal colour, type size, corner radius, shadow or duration in `site.css` — grepped, and a
  literal fails the build (SC-014). The fix is a new variable in the emitter, never a value here;
- recreating an application component that has no documentation counterpart — no overflow menu, no
  chips, no worktree list (FR-029b);
- a `@font-face`, stylesheet, script or image from any host but the site's own (FR-031, SC-015);
- substituting a colour that fails contrast. The publication fails instead, and the token is fixed
  (FR-033).

## Scheme selection

`data-scheme` on the root element follows the reader's `prefers-color-scheme` by default and can be
overridden by the site's own toggle, persisted locally. Both schemes are checked for WCAG 2.2 AA on
every publication (FR-027a, SC-013), and a screenshot taken in a scheme is shown on a page in the
same scheme (FR-032).

## The contrast gate

`crates/micold-core/tests/site_theme_contrast.rs` asserts, over the emitted set, that every
foreground/background pair the site actually uses meets WCAG 2.2 AA — 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for
large text and for UI component boundaries — in both schemes. It names the offending token when it
fails. It runs in the ordinary suite, so the failure lands in the change that moved the token
(FR-033), before the publication that would otherwise have discovered it.
